transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. A small amount of clean water left in the bottom of the tub under the filter is actually normal. Dishwashers are not designed to be 100% bone dry; this residual water keeps the internal seals from drying out and cracking. If you scoop that water up with a cup or sponge, it should disappear completely. However, if there is a large volume of dirty water left over (more than just a splash), or if the dishes are coming out wet and soapy, then it isn't draining properly. To check this, please twist and lift out the filter assembly at the bottom of the tub. Is there only a small amount of clean water in the sump underneath, or is there a much larger volume of dirty water?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
Thanks, I've taken the filter out. It's just a small amount of clean water in the sump under the filter, roughly a cupful, and none in the main tub. The filter itself looks clean.

That suggests it is working normally. A small amount of clean water (about a cupful) left in the sump under the filter after a cycle is standard for dishwashers; it keeps the internal seals lubricated and prevents them from drying out.

candidates: Normal residual water in the sump (high)
Blocked filter or drain path (debris, kinked hose) (medium)
